title: Synchronization induced by stochastic subsystem resetting in complex networks
abstract: We study synchronization in network-coupled oscillators subject to stochastic resetting of a subset of nodes. We show that resetting can induce collective coherence in oscillators that are never directly reset, through the interplay of network structure, frequency heterogeneity, and the organization of the reset subsystem. In the infinite-resetting-rate limit, the reset nodes become effectively pinned to a reference phase, and linearization near synchronization maps the dynamics of the remaining subsystem onto a grounded-Laplacian problem. This formulation yields an analytical relation between the synchronization level and the reset parameters, providing an estimate of the coupling strength required to achieve a prescribed degree of coherence. Beyond the linear regime, we develop a mean-field description in which the reset subsystem acts as an effective ordering field for the remaining oscillators. Numerical simulations across different network topologies confirm these predictions and show that synchronization is enhanced by increasing both the reset fraction and network connectivity. In heterogeneous networks, the placement of reset nodes can strongly influence the synchronization response. For frequency distributions with nonzero mean, resetting competes with the intrinsic collective rotation and can drive the system from a rotating synchronized state to a phase-locked state. These results establish subsystem resetting as a mechanism for inducing and controlling collective synchronization in complex networks.
summary: This paper analyzes how stochastic resetting of nodes in a complex network can induce and control collective synchronization in coupled oscillators. By analyzing the system in the infinite-rate limit, the authors derive analytical relations connecting coherence to network structure and reset parameters. The work establishes resetting as a powerful mechanism for controlling collective dynamics, potentially leading to phase-locked states.
main_problem: The study investigates how stochastic resetting of a subset of nodes affects the collective synchronization of coupled oscillators on a complex network.
main_result: Resetting can induce collective coherence in oscillators that are never directly reset, and this mechanism can drive the system from a rotating synchronized state to a phase-locked state.
method: The analysis employs linearization near synchronization, mapping the dynamics to a grounded-Laplacian problem, and developing a mean-field description for the non-linear regime.
model_or_system: The model uses network-coupled oscillators governed by a generalized Kuramoto model on a network defined by an adjacency matrix. The system is divided into a reset subsystem and a non-reset subsystem.
key_observables: Synchronization level/coherence, global order parameter, and collective angular velocity (to distinguish between phase-locked and rotating states).
important_parameters: Resetting fraction, network connectivity, frequency heterogeneity, and the infinite-resetting-rate limit ($\lambda ightarrow \infty$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the infinite-resetting-rate limit and assumes the network is undirected and connected.
figures_summary: Figures characterize the time evolution of the order parameter and phase, showing transitions between stationary (phase locked) and rotating synchronization regimes based on reset fraction and connectivity.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the system and the role of resetting, to deriving analytical results in the infinite-rate limit using Laplacian formulations, and finally developing a mean-field theory to characterize the transition between different synchronization states.
why_interesting: The concept of an external, non-local intervention (resetting) inducing global order is analogous to external driving fields or engineered coupling in quantum systems, providing a control mechanism for collective quantum states.
